newsitem.title: UK: Boots buys skincare group for 115 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: Boots buys skincare group for 115 mln stg.

text.p: The Boots Company Plc said it had bought French company Laboratoires Lutsia from Roussel Uclaf for 920 million French francs, equivalent to 115 million stg.
It said in a statement that the price included repayment within the next five days of inter-company debt amounting to some 50 million francs.

Boots said the acquisition, for its Boots Healthcare International (BHI) unit, would give BHI total sales in France of 460 million francs, or 57.5 million stg, and boost total BHI skincare sales to over 75 million stg in a full year.
Boots said in a statement that BHI planned "significant expansion" of Lutsia's Lutsine and Onagrine skincare ranges to "fulfil...(their) international potential."

Lutsine is an anti-acne product while Onagrine is anti-ageing. Boots said sales of the two products in France were 315 million francs or 39.4 million stg in 1995, when it had sales growth of some 11 percent.
Lutsia employs over 200 people, Boots said.

Boots said the deal was in line with BHI plans to build businesses in each major European marketplace, particularly in its core products -- analgesics under the Nurofen brand, cough and throat cures such as Strepsils and skincare.
Boots said after the deal, these three product areas would account for over 60 percent of BHI sales.
Lutsia has a seven percent share of French skincare products which are sold only through pharmacies.
BHI will use the Lutsia sales force to promote its own brands of skincare while its own sales team will focus on Nurofen and Strepsils.
Lutsia head office staff will move to BHI's French headquarters.
"Together Lutsia and BHI will create a formidable business," BHI managing director Barry Clare said.
"Beyond France there is real potential for growth," he said.
